```{r setup, include=FALSE}
root<-normalizePath(getwd())
while(!file.exists(file.path(root,'_quarto.yml')))root<-dirname(root)
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_presentation.R'))
p<-load_presentation(root)
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_aggregate_presentation.R'))
a<-load_aggregate_presentation(root)
mirror_presentation_csv(root,p$out)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.retina=1)
stopifnot(all(p$obj$rows$half=='A'))
```

## Summary and downloads {.unnumbered #downloads}

[Return to the visual summary](3.1a.2_heldout_exploration.html).
Every report-level results table below includes its full set of targets, cutoffs and missing policies, with column filters, pages of 25 rows, two-decimal numeric display, and a **Download filtered CSV** button. cat(paste0('- [',gsub('_',' ',sub('[.]csv$','',files)),'](output/3.1a/',files,')',collapse='\n'),'\n')

## Data: how much did the new target recover? {#data}

The complete five-year window is retained as a sensitivity. Available years need not be contiguous. The k distribution uses all pseudo-treated half-A rows as its denominator, including k = 0; plotted bars therefore need not sum to the full height when only k = 1–5 are drawn.

```{r k-figure, fig.cap='Shares of all half-A county/simulation rows with one through five usable post years. Rows with no usable post year are reported in the full table.', fig.height=4.5}
v<-ordered_plot(p$kd[k>=1]);v[,k:=factor(k)]
ggplot(v,aes(model,share,fill=k))+geom_col()+facet_wrap(~scenario,nrow=1)+
 scale_fill_brewer(palette='Blues',name='Available years')+scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::label_percent())+
 labs(x=NULL,y='Share of all rows')+presentation_theme()+theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1))
```

## Methods and definitions {.unnumbered #methods}

### Saved data and scope

The input is physically half A only and `half == "A"` is asserted before use. The assignment hash is checked against the saved assignment; the seed and size stratification are unchanged. All fitted models and original statistical outputs are preserved. This presentation reads the existing result CSVs and fails if they predate the revised A-only input; refresh the original computation report before presenting refreshed data.

The main saved fits use `r` (simulation), `i` (county), `year`, `start_year_sim`, `y`, `y0_hat`, and `y0_post_1`–`y0_post_200`. Event time is `year - start_year_sim`. County checkpoints use `sim`, `id`, `x`, `model`, `scenario`, `mu_ho_mean`, `mu_ho_var`, `ppp_ho_upper`, `ppp_ho_lower`, `y_post`, `mu_post_mean`, `pre_rmse` and `pre_rms_pearson`.

### Targets and diagnostics

For event years 0–4, retain finite observed and expected counts with a strictly positive expected count. If **k ≥ 1**, `err_raw = abs(sum(y) - sum(mu))` and `err_z = err_raw / sqrt(sum(mu))`. This is the absolute error of the cumulative sum: errors may cancel across years. Available years need not be contiguous. `h0` uses the first post year; `k5` preserves the original complete-five-year eligibility, including nonnegative yearly means. Available-window county averages use k ≥ 2 by default; their replication counts are saved. Both new and complete-window county averages include the current simulation when eligible, are explanatory, and still contain sampling noise. An average target can label a simulation with k = 0, evaluated in its own stratum.

Diagnostics are pre-period RMSE, RMS Pearson residual, held-out raw error, held-out error divided by `sqrt(mu_ho_mean)`, and held-out error divided by `sqrt(mu_ho_mean + mu_ho_var)`. Scores take absolute values, except predictive surprise uses `1 - p_two`.

Mid-p divides equality mass evenly between the tails: `p_upper = P(Y > y) + 0.5 P(Y = y)`, `p_lower = P(Y < y) + 0.5 P(Y = y)`, and `p_two = min(1, 2 min(p_upper, p_lower))`. Paired legacy inclusive tails are converted exactly; a lone tail is unavailable. Discrete mid-p is not exactly uniform even for a correctly specified count model.

### Predictive coverage

The saved `y0_post_*` columns are expected-count draws, rather than predictive observed-count draws. Preparation adds seeded independent Poisson observation noise conditional on each latent draw, preserves matching draw indices across years, and sums predictions over the same available window. Empirical type-7 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles define the interval. No yearly quantiles are added and no model is refitted. Invalid latent or predictive draws make coverage unavailable while point targets remain usable. Coverage counts and missing shares are reported separately; per-year quantiles alone are rejected.

### Within-simulation evaluation and Monte Carlo uncertainty

Spearman correlation, AUC and top-decile class membership are computed within scenario × model × simulation × k. The target boundary is defined before diagnostic availability is applied; ties on the boundary are positives. Skip strata with fewer than five paired rows or one outcome class; constant scores make correlation unavailable. Valid k statistics are weighted by usable stratum size, then simulations are averaged equally. Pooled results remain available.

MC SE is `sd(statistic across finite simulations) / sqrt(number of finite simulations)`. It describes simulation uncertainty, not independence of repeated county rows. Retention screening uses strict diagnostic thresholds; equality is retained. Pre-RMSE top-percent screens use the nearest requested number of finite-diagnostic counties, with county ID breaking ties. Missing diagnostics are kept or excluded in separately labelled variants.

### Random-band correction {#band-correction}

**This is the only statistical computation changed for the presentation revision.** The previous plotted bounds were averages of each simulation's 2.5% and 97.5% random-reduction quantiles. They described a typical simulation's spread, not the spread of an average across simulations.

The correction regenerates the same 100 seeded permutations per simulation, with the same county ordering, eligible errors and excluded counts. Every regenerated per-simulation random mean is checked against the saved mean. For each draw index, reductions are first averaged across finite simulations; quantiles are then taken across those draw-index averages. The point estimates for actual screening, calibration, coverage, associations and ranks are unchanged. The old band columns remain preserved in the original result CSVs.

The per-rule corrected table matches each rule's actual excluded count in every simulation. The **single grey plotting band** uses a common excluded-fraction grid, rounding that fraction to the nearest county count in each simulation; this removes duplicated diagnostic-specific ribbons. It is a random-screening reference distribution, not a confidence interval for the observed screening benefit.

```{r width-example}
v<-p$bands[model=='RW' & scenario=='MAR' & target=='err_z' & diagnostic=='p_two' & cutoff==.05 & missing_handling=='keep',
 .(Model=model,Scenario=scenario,`Old band width`=old_width,`Corrected band width`=new_width)]
gt::gt(as.data.frame(v)) |> gt::fmt_percent(columns=c(`Old band width`,`Corrected band width`),decimals=2)
```

[All width comparisons CSV](output/3.1a/random_band_width_comparison.csv)

```{r width-comparison-table}
full_dt(p,'random_band_width_comparison')
```

## Does screening improve the aggregate estimate? {#aggregate}

### Estimand, screens and intervals

For each subgroup × scenario × model × simulation, let R be the retained counties with at least one usable event year 0–4. Define

<div class="callout callout-style-simple callout-note">
<p><em>E</em><sub>R</sub> = (1 / |R|) × Σ<sub>i∈R</sub> Σ<sub>t∈Wᵢ</sub> (y<sub>it</sub> − μ̂<sub>it</sub>)</p>
<p><em>Z</em><sub>R</sub> = <em>E</em><sub>R</sub> / √[Σ<sub>i∈R</sub> Σ<sub>t∈Wᵢ</sub> μ̂<sub>it</sub> / |R|²]</p>
</div>

County signs are retained. The existing rule grid and missing-diagnostic policies determine retention using pre-treatment diagnostics only. Pre-RMSE percentile thresholds use the original full A pool, then the noncore restriction is applied; this keeps retained counts directly comparable to the existing analysis. Noncore is `urb == "6.NonCore"` in `data/notpublic/compact_dt.rds`; no proxy is used. Model fits remain unchanged.

The 200 seeded Poisson predictive draws reproduce the existing county intervals exactly. Draw b is averaged across retained counties after summing matching yearly draw indices; type-7 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles give the aggregate interval. An invalid predictive county makes its retained-set interval unavailable without removing it from the point estimate. Interval availability and finite simulation counts are exported explicitly. An empty retained set gives unavailable metrics, rather than a zero error.

Across simulations, RMSE is `sqrt(mean(E^2))`; bias is `mean(E)` and MAE is `mean(abs(E))`. Each mean has an empirical MC SE. RMSE MC SE uses the delta method on squared errors. The ratio MC SE uses the paired influence values `(E_rule^2 - ratio^2 E_base^2)/(2 ratio mean(E_base^2))`, divided by the square root of the number of paired finite simulations. The standardized aggregate metrics use Z. Baseline comparisons use the same paired simulations. **Relative aggregate RMSE** divides `sqrt(mean(E^2))` by `mean(retained observed aggregate)` within subgroup × scenario × model × rule × missing policy, using simulations where both values are finite. It is not the mean of simulation-level ratios. Its MC SE uses the joint delta-method influence `(E^2 - mean(E^2))/(2 RMSE mean(Y)) - RMSE (Y - mean(Y))/mean(Y)^2`, retaining the numerator/denominator covariance. Nonpositive observed means yield an unavailable relative metric.

**All-A absolute RMSE ratios are affected by dropping large counties.** The relative metric makes the retained outcome scale explicit, while screening still changes the estimand. Both relative RMSE and its MC SE are displayed alongside the absolute ratio in each subgroup's scorecard and full summary.

Random exclusions retain exactly the rule's county count within each subgroup and simulation. Each of 100 seeded permutations defines nested retained sets across cutoffs. Squared aggregate errors are averaged across simulations by draw index, then divided by the corresponding paired unscreened MSE and square-rooted; the band is the 2.5%–97.5% quantiles across those 100 ratios. It is not a significance interval for the diagnostic rule.

The **infeasible single-pass standardized-variance oracle** estimates each county's variance of `(sum_y - sum_mu) / sqrt(sum_mu)` using only its other eligible simulations. In the current simulation/subgroup it computes one threshold, `2 * mean(v_i over all eligible counties)`, and excludes variances above it. **There is no iteration and no recomputation over the retained set.** Scaling avoids directly ranking counties by raw count variance. Actual aggregate RMSE can still reflect bias, dependence and available-window composition. A model/scenario/subgroup oracle cell is shown in the main figures and scorecards only if no available replication excludes more than 40%; all cells remain in the details table, with mean/max excluded shares and visibility flags. When any eligible county has fewer than two other usable simulations, its LOSO variance is unavailable and the entire oracle replication is marked unavailable; no variance is guessed and that replication is excluded from the paired oracle comparison. `n_oracle_unavailable`, `n_error` and `paired_n_sims` report this limitation. It is not a claim of global optimality or an operational screening rule. [Crump, Hotz, Imbens and Mitnik (2009)](https://scholar.harvard.edu/sites/scholar.harvard.edu/files/imbens/files/dealing_with_limited_overlap_in_estimation_of_average_treatment_effects.pdf) motivate precision-oriented trimming. Inverse-variance weighting is omitted because it would change the estimand further.

The exploratory minimum flags use `ratio + 1.96 * MC_SE < 1`. They are pointwise, not adjusted for selecting a cutoff or for multiple comparisons. Screening defines the estimand as counties with reliably predictable untreated outcomes; section 7 describes excluded counties. No rule is selected, and the decision file remains unchanged. No half-B evaluation input is read.

The manuscript comparison's available-window reference applies its unweighted county-average formula directly to saved yearly predictions restricted to A. The complete-window reference keeps counties with all five usable event years and therefore is a sensitivity comparison, not an equality check for the new available-window estimand. Published all-county manuscript RMSE is not directly comparable to a fixed half-A subset. The reported per-replication equality is stronger than an agreement within MC error for the matched available-window reference.

Size-stratum population ranges are the minimum/maximum of county mean **pre-adoption** outcome-age population (`n`) among the original half-A county assignment; they describe actual populations but are not the stratum-defining variable. The strata are quintiles of mean pre-period expected counts; stratum 5 is largest on that defining measure. Ranges overlap because population and expected count differ.


[Manuscript comparison by replication](output/3.1a/aggregate_manuscript_per_simulation.csv)


::: {.callout-important}
**The complete-five-year manuscript reference does not reproduce the available-window baseline within Monte Carlo error.** Agreement holds in `r sum(a$manuscript_comparison$complete_window_agrees_within_mc_error)` of `r nrow(a$manuscript_comparison)` subgroup/model/scenario comparisons, using a paired 1.96-MC-SE difference check. The available-window analysis includes partial post-period histories and uses a different county denominator; its matched-window formula check is exact. The original manuscript-window reference is exported separately, and the requested available-year target is preserved. These results therefore support the available-window aggregate estimand rather than a replication of the manuscript's complete-horizon numerical RMSE.
:::

### Same base population as TWFE {#twfe-common}

```{r twfe-common-details-setup, include=FALSE}
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_twfe_population_presentation.R'))
common_sens<-load_twfe_common_population(root)
common_csv<-list(read=function(n)fread(file.path(common_sens$out,paste0(n,'.csv'))))
```

This additive sensitivity derives E directly from the saved **A-only TWFE available-window fit cache** for each scenario and simulation: `k >= 1`, finite observed and predicted cumulative totals, and positive predicted total. Cached source path, bytes, modification time, input timestamp and assignment hash are checked. The resulting membership must exactly match the prepared finite TWFE target IDs. Only A-only fit caches, the A input, assignment metadata and county metadata immediately restricted to A are used; no half-B evaluation file or complete-panel saved fit is deserialized by this step. Missing/stale caches or ambiguous membership stop the run.

Every model must have a finite target for every E county, with the same available-year count and observed total as TWFE. No model-specific intersection is silently substituted. Noncore uses E intersected with the original `urb == "6.NonCore"` indicator; all-A is secondary. Each model's original full-A calibrated screen is applied to its E counties: diagnostics, full rule grid, missing policies, percentile reference, rounding and tie-breaker are preserved. Outcomes are aggregated on E only; screened populations can again differ. This preserves all original TWFE results and guarantees that retained E counts cannot exceed the original counts.

Signed and standardized aggregate errors, 200 matching seeded Poisson predictive draw indices, type-7 95% intervals, RMSE, relative RMSE, covariance-aware relative MC SE, paired RMSE-ratio MC SE, coverage, width, counts and excluded shares reuse the existing section-10 formulas. The 100 seeded random exclusions match each rule's retained count on E (TWFE reuses its original draws because its population and screens are identical); MSE is averaged across simulations by random draw index before taking RMSE ratios and quantile bands. The original results are used only as faint visual references and remain saved unchanged.

C consists of each non-TWFE model's eligible noncore counties absent from E. Its observed zero-history checkpoint audit is exported; membership is never inferred from that history flag. The full/E/C table includes the mean C share and MC SE, denominators and finite counts. Replications with empty C have unavailable C errors and intervals. Weighted identities for observed aggregates and signed errors are checked replication by replication; component RMSEs are not additive.

The common unscreened county IDs/counts and observed aggregates match across all six models for every simulation/scenario. TWFE's metrics for every rule and both missing policies reproduce the original section 10, and every model/rule's retained E count is bounded by its original count, the decomposition's full noncore metrics reproduce every non-TWFE original baseline, and decomposition E metrics reproduce the common sensitivity baseline. A-only/ID/hash checks run at entry and exit. Checksums preserve every original CSV and the decision file. An explicit Unscreened row is added to the existing scorecard from saved baseline results, and all prior scorecard rows remain unchanged.

### Same screened sample for the aggregate estimand {#aggregate-common-screen}

```{r common-screen-details-setup, include=FALSE}
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_common_screen_presentation.R'))
common_screen<-load_aggregate_common_screen(root)
```

The base is the saved TWFE-eligible **noncore E** from section 10.1. Each scenario/simulation's E county IDs are aligned across all six models; available-year counts and observed targets must agree. For |z| > 2, mid-p < 0.05 and mid-p < 0.10, each model's own section-10 screen is evaluated on E, then the retained masks are combined with the same `Reduce(&, screens)` intersection used in section 8. These fixed thresholds reproduce section 10.1's own retained counts exactly. Both missing-kept and missing-excluded policies are computed separately. Unscreened means all of E and is included once per model/scenario/simulation.

Signed error, absolute and relative RMSE, their MC SEs, the paired ratio to unscreened E and its MC SE, matching seeded predictive draw indices, type-7 95% aggregate predictive intervals, coverage, width, retained counts and excluded shares reuse section 10's formulas. Model parameters and saved predictive draws are unchanged. An empty intersection is recorded with zero retained counties and unavailable errors/intervals; finite counts are reported rather than imputing zero errors.

Single-model contributions count counties flagged only by that model. Pooled unique contributions sum exclusive counts over simulations and divide by pooled common-screen exclusion counts. Mean per-simulation contributions and their MC SEs are also exported, assigning share zero if that simulation excludes no counties. Shared exclusions have flags from two or more models and are counted once. The six pooled unique shares plus the shared share sum to one. Contributions describe overlapping flags; they are not causal attribution.

The per-model subset audit retains explicit common county-ID keys, the own-screen and common retained counts, and the original section-10.1 retained count. All common counts are bounded by every own count; the independently recomputed own masks reproduce the saved 10.1 counts. The equality audit checks IDs and observed aggregates across all six models. The membership export lists retained counties once per scenario/simulation/rule/policy. Only the prepared half-A input, validated A-only saved-fit caches and saved A-only eligibility exports are loaded; no half-B evaluation file or complete-panel fit is opened. A-only/hash checks run at entry and exit, and checksums preserve all previous CSVs and the decision template.
